sentences.text:
The Hon'Ble Sri Justice E.V.Venugopal
 Criminal Petition No.5309 Of 2020
Order:

1 This criminal petition, under Section 482 Cr.P.C, is filed seeking to quash the proceedings against the petitioners/A.2 and A.3 in C.C.No.200 of 2020 on the file of the Court of the learned V Additional Metropolitan Magistrate, Ranga Reddy District, registered for the offences punishable under Sections 498-A IPC and Sections 3 and 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act.

entities.text: V Additional Metropolitan Magistrate, Ranga Reddy District
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2 Heard Sri Midhun Kumar, learned counsel representing Sri Vankina Allu, learned counsel for the petitioners, Sri Syed Yaser Mamoon, learned Additional Public Prosecutor, for respondent Nos.1 and 2 - State and Sri T.Surya Satish, learned counsel for the third respondent.
3 Petitioner No.1 herein (A.2) is the mother and Petitioner No.2 herein (A.3) is the elder brother of one Ranjit Kumar (A.1).

The facts that lead to the filing of the present criminal petition, as per the complaint lodged by the third respondent herein, in nutshell, are that the marriage of the third respondent was performed with one Ranjit Kumar - A.1 in the above case on 26.5.2009.
The parents of the third respondent gave Rs.30.00 lakhs cash, 60 tulas of gold and 5 kgs of silver to the accused on demand towards dowry.
After the marriage, the third respondent joined the matrimonial house for leading conjugal life with A.1.
After one month A.1 to A.3 started harassing the third respondent physically and mentally demanding additional dowry.
Out of the wedlock the third respondent and the A.1 were blessed with a male child on 19.11.2011.

After that the petitioners and A.1 continued harassing the third respondent on one pretext or the other and on 29.11.2012 due to the unbearable harassment,
third respondent went to her parents' house.
The petitioners and A.1 did not allow the third respondent into the matrimonial home when her father in law died.
Though the third respondent staged dharna in front of the house of the petitioners from 28th March to 10th May, they did not allow her inside the house.
Later the third respondent stayed in the ground floor of the same house till 05.7.2019.
But the petitioners got evicted her from there through Court orders.
The accused also harassed the third respondent by approaching Human Rights Commission making various allegations against her.
The petitioners did not provide her basic amenities and education aid to the son of the third respondent.
A.1 filed FCOP No.534 of 2013 on the file of the Family Court, Ranga Reddy District and obtained divorce.
Thus, the accused subjected the third respondent to cruelty both mental and physical and hence they are liable for prosecution under the above Sections law.

The police, after conducting due investigation, filed charge sheet before the learned trial Court,
which was taken on file for the offences punishable under Sections 498-A of IPC and Sections 3 and 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act.
As stated supra, seeking to quash the said proceedings, the petitioners who are A.2 and A.3 filed the present criminal petition.

4 Learned counsel for the petitioners advanced his arguments mainly contending that the third respondent used to deter the petitioners and her husband (A.1) to kill their child and gave threats of filing criminal cases.

The third respondent threatened the life and limb of the petitioners herein and also the husband of the first petitioner and illegally blocked the entrance to their house and as such G.Radha Devi vs The State Of Telangana on 30 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/28526276/

sentences.text: the petitioners obtained police protection by way of filing writ petition before this Hon'ble Court.
It is his predominant contention that the third respondent started filing criminal cases out of vengeance after a period of eight years of her leaving the marital home.

The third respondent staged dharna in front of the house of the petitioners from 28th March to 10th May and later stayed in the ground floor of the same house till 05.7.2019 by blocking the entrance thereby caused lot of inconvenience for the ingress and aggress of the petitioners to their own house.

The vehement contention of the learned counsel for the petitioners is that the third respondent never lived in the shared house of the petitioners along with her husband for a long time and after lapse of eight years of her leaving the marital home, she lodged the present complaint that too after the Family Court granted divorce with an ulterior and oblique motive.
The allegations made in the complaint, if they are taken in entirety, are all omnibus and they do not constitute any offence much less the offences alleged against the petitioners.

He lastly contended that the second petitioner herein was working in Bangalore from the year 2005 till 2012 and came back to Hyderabad only in January, 2013 to take care of his father who was also harassed and threatened by the third respondent.
He was living separately at a different house in Hyderabad and he came to the present house only after the third respondent was legally evicted through Court orders from the subject premises.

5 The learned counsel for the petitioners relied on the ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the following judgments: Sushil Kumar Sharma vs. Union of India 1, Swapnil vs. State of Madhya Pradesh 2 and Kamlesh Kalra vs. Shilpika Kalra 3, in support of his contentions.

entities.text: Sushil Kumar Sharma vs. Union of India 1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Swapnil vs. State of Madhya Pradesh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 6 On the other hand, the learned Additional Public Prosecutor submitted that all the accused have filed a petition under Section 239 Cr.P.C, before the learned trial Court, seeking discharge and the learned (2005) 6 SCC 281 (2014) 13 SCC 567 2020 SCC OnLine SC 1493 trial Court has dismissed the said petition.

In that view of the matter, truth or otherwise will come out only after a full fledged trial and this is not a fit case to entertain the present petition at this premature stage and prayed to dismiss this petition.

7 In Sushil Kumar Sharma (1 supra) the Hon'ble Supreme Court held as follows:
"19.
The object of the provision is prevention of the dowry menace.
But as has been rightly contented by the petitioner many instances have come to light where the complaints are not bonafide and have been filed with oblique motive.
In such cases acquittal of the accused does not in all cases wipe out the anomy suffered during and prior to trial.
Sometimes adverse media coverage adds to the misery.

The question,
therefore, is what remedial measures can be taken to prevent abuse of the well-intentioned provision.
Merely because the provision is constitutional and intra vires, does not give a licence to unscrupulous persons to wreck personal vendetta or unleash harassment.
It may, therefore, become necessary for the legislature to find out ways how the makers of frivolous complaints or allegations can be appropriately dealt with.
Till then the Courts have to take care of the situation within the existing frame work.
As noted above the object is to strike at the roots of dowry menace.
But by misuse of the provision a new legal terrorism can be unleashed.
The provision is intended to be used a shield and not an assassin's weapon.

If cry of "wolf" is made too G.Radha Devi vs The State Of Telangana on 30 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/28526276/
2 often as a prank assistance and protection may not be available when the actual "wolf" appears.

sentences.text: There is no question of investigating agency and Courts casually dealing with the allegations.
They cannot follow any straitjacket formula in the matters relating to dowry tortures, deaths and cruelty.
It cannot be lost sight of that ultimate objective of every legal system is to arrive at truth, punish the guilty and protect the innocent.
There is no scope for any pre-conceived notion or view.

It is strenuously argued by the petitioner that the investigating agencies and the courts start with the presumptions that the accused persons are guilty and that the complainant is speaking the truth.
This is too wide available and generalized statement.
Certain statutory presumptions are drawn which again are rebuttable.
It is to be noted that the role of the investigating agencies and the courts is that of watch dog and not of a bloodhound.
It should be their effort to see that an innocent person is not made to suffer on account of unfounded, baseless and malicious allegations.
It is equally undisputable that in many cases no direct evidence is available and the courts have to act on circumstantial evidence.
While dealing with such cases, the law laid down relating to circumstantial evidence has to be kept in view."

8 In Swapnil vs. State of Madhya Pradesh (2 supra) the Hon'ble Supreme Court held as follows:
"10.

entities.text: Swapnil vs. State of Madhya Pradesh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The first Appellant and second Respondent had in fact solemnized their marriage at Arya Samaj Mandir on 16.06.2007 privately, as they were stated to be in love with each other for sometime.
Thereafter only, in the presence of the family members, marriage was solemnized on 24.06.2009.
It has to be seen that admittedly the second Respondent has been living separately since April, 2011.
Thereafter, she had lodged a complaint on 07.09.2011 before the very same police station.
The same was duly enquired into and it was closed stating that the dispute is actually between the families which are to be otherwise settled in legal proceedings.

If there are such differences between families which are to be settled in legal proceedings, how such differences would constitute and give rise to a successful prosecution Under Sections 498A or 506 Indian Penal Code or Under Section 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act,
1961, is the crucial question.

11. The second Respondent has been living separately since April, 2011 and hence,
there is no question of any beating by the Appellants as alleged by her.

The relationship having got strained ever since April, 2011, even application for restitution of conjugal rights having been withdrawn on 16.04.2012 as the second Respondent was not interested to live together, it is difficult to believe that there is still a demand for dowry on 30.04.2012 coupled with criminal intimidation.
The allegations are vague and bereft of the details as to the place and the time of the incident.
We had called for the records and have gone through the same.

The materials before the learned Judicial Magistrate First Class, Indore are not sufficient to form an opinion that there is ground for presuming that the accused Appellants have committed the offence under the charged Sections.

The Additional Sessions Court and the High Court missed these crucial points while considering the petition G.Radha Devi vs The State Of Telangana on 30 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/28526276/
3 filed by the Appellants Under Section 397 and Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure respectively.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The veiled object behind the lame prosecution is apparently to harass the Appellants.
We are, hence, of the view that the impugned prosecution is wholly unfounded......"

9 In Kamlesh Kalra case (3 supra) the Hon'ble Supreme Court held as follows:
19.

In view of the aforesaid facts, we are of the opinion that the allegations of the complainant-Shilpika Kalra with regard to non-return of the Stridhan articles and the charges Under Section 406 against the Kamlesh Kalra (or even against Manish Kalra,
Avnish Kalra and Suman Kalra) are not sustainable in law.

It clearly appears that the filing of the criminal complaint is a pressure tactic, having been employed by the complainant-Shilpika Kalra against her husband, mother-in-law, brother-in-law and sister-in-law, which is clearly an abuse of the process of Court, and is liable to be quashed in toto.
10 Let me consider the facts of the case in touch stone of the principle laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the above cases.

11 The petitioners contend that some time after the marriage, the third respondent started harassing the accused threatening that she will consume sleeping pills and she will also kill their child and she behaved unendurable which caused havoc and one cannot live with her peacefully.

As seen from the record it is manifest that the third respondent filed a complaint with WPS, Saroornagar Police Station, previously also against the petitioners/accused and the police conducted counselling between the parties.
On that, the said case was closed as not pressed and thereafter the third respondent left the matrimonial home of the petitioners / accused on 29.11.2012.
The present complaint was lodged on 20.12.2019 i.e. after long lapse of seven years.
Except alleging that the petitioners demanded costly articles and other items on every festive occasion the third respondent has not placed any material on record to substantiate the same.
Hence, this Court has no other option except to cloth the said allegations as omnibus and baseless allegations.

12 As per Rule 5 of the Dowry Prohibition Rules, 1998, every complaint shall be made by the aggrieved party itself or any other person on behalf of the aggrieved party either on the demand of dowry or accepting dowry within a period of one year.

Rule 10 thereof stipulates that any offence under Section 3 and 4 or any dispute under Section 6 of the Act shall be filed before expiry of one year and the same shall be finalised within two years from the date of filing.

13 In the present case,
admittedly, the marriage of the third respondent was solemnised with the first accused on 26.5.2009 and it is also an admitted fact that the third respondent left the matrimonial home of the accused on 29.11.2012.

14 It is borne out of the record that because of the Dharna staged by the third respondent the petitioners could not enter into their own house and the said dharna was publicised in print and electronic media.

Because of the harassment and having not able to bear with the torture meted out by the third respondent, the husband of the third respondent filed FCOP No.534 of 2013 on the file of the Judge, Family Court, Ranga Reddy and the said O.P was allowed dissolving the marriage between the third respondent and the first accused by decree of divorce dated 24.11.2017.
Thereafter the third respondent instituted the present case.

sentences.text: It is pertinent to observe that the third respondent made unfounded allegations against the petitioners and her husband which amounts to mental cruelty on the part of the third respondent herself.

The learned Family Court, on an elaborate discussion of the pleadings and contentions, observed that cruelty is on the part of the third respondent herself but not on the part of the petitioners and accordingly granted decree of divorce and that the third respondent failed to prove the alleged illegal demands and harassment.
The allegations are vague and bereft of the details as to the place and the time of the incident.

The materials before the learned trial Court are not sufficient to form an opinion that there is ground for presuming that the accused petitioners have committed the offence under the alleged Sections of law.
15 The contents of the F.I.R. also reveal that general allegations are levelled against the petitioners herein and no specific and distinct allegations are made against them.
In the absence of any specific role attributed to the petitioners herein it would be unjust if they are forced to go through the tribulations of the trial.
The allegations are general and omnibus.

Insofar as husband is concerned,
since he is not here this Court has not examined the veracity of allegations made against him.
However, as far as the petitioners herein are concerned, the allegations made against them being general and omnibus, do not warrant prosecution.

The expression 'cruelty' in Section 498-A IPC covers the conduct which may drive the woman to commit suicide or cause grave injury (mental or physical) or danger to life or harassment with a view to coerce her to meet unlawful demand is absent in the present case.

In Arnesh Kumar v. State of Bihar 4 the Hon'ble Supreme Court held as follows:
"There is phenomenal increase in matrimonial disputes in recent years.

entities.text: Arnesh Kumar v. State of Bihar
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The institution of marriage is greatly revered in this country.
Section 498-A of the Indian Penal Code was introduced with avowed object to combat the menace of (2014) 8 SCC 273 harassment to a woman at the hands of her husband and his relatives.
The fact that Section 498-A is a cognizable and non-bailable offence has lent it a dubious place of pride amongst the provisions that are used as weapons rather than shield by disgruntled wives.
The simplest way to harass is to get the husband and his relatives arrested under this provision.
In a quite number of cases, bed-ridden grand-fathers and grand-mothers of the husbands, their sisters living abroad for decades are arrested."
16 From the above it is clear that the relatives of the husband should not be roped in on the basis of omnibus allegations unless specific instances of their involvement in the crime are made out.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court in Priyanka Jaiswal Vs. The State of Jharkhand and Ors. 5 held that mere allegations which are omnibus and without any specific allegation of overt act imputed against the accused should be deprecated.

entities.text: Priyanka Jaiswal Vs. The State of Jharkhand and Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 17 As held by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in State of Haryana V. Bhajan Lal 6 where a criminal proceeding is manifestly attended with mala fide and / or where the proceeding is maliciously instituted with an ulterior motive for wreaking vengeance on the accused and with a view to spite him due to private and personal grudge, then the criminal prosecution can be quashed against the accused.

entities.text: State of Haryana V. Bhajan Lal 6

sentences.text:
From an analysis of the above discussion and in the light of the principles enunciated by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the cases cited MANU/SC/0359/2024 1992 SCC (Cri) 426 supra, this Court is of the considered view that the third respondent failed to make out any case to continue the prosecution against the petitioners under the above sated Sections of law and hence the petitioners deserve the relief sought for.
19

Accordingly, this criminal petition is allowed, quashing the proceedings against the petitioners/A.2 and A.3 in C.C.No.200 of 2020 on the file of the Court of the learned V Additional Metropolitan Magistrate, Ranga Reddy District.
20 Miscellaneous petitions if any pending in this criminal petition shall stand closed.

E.V.VENUGOPAL, J.
